text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Suharto of Indonesia says civil and political rights have no meaning to a citizen if he lacks an education or a job, defending his government's emphasis on economic growth.
- United States says it will continue official-level contacts with Taiwan, as visiting senior US official offers help to get Taiwan into World Trade Organisation.
- Astronaut Shannon Lucid, after six months in orbit, is one step closer to earth as shuttle Atlantis roars into space to pick her up from Russia's Mir station.
- Suzhou Industrial Park, Singapore's regional project, is working on likely investments of US$1.5 billion.
- Neptune Orient Lines reports 43 per cent plunge in interim net earnings to Singapore $10.2 million and would consider a merger with another shipping company if it found a like-minded partner.
- 1.53 million Singaporeans have been allocated 804 million Singapore Telecom second-tranche shares at S$2.50 a share.
- Share price of Sea View Hotel Ltd jumps to record S$15.50 on talk of a possible takeover by First Capital Corporation.

- Cam International Holdings Ltd sold 52.5 per cent of its subsidiary Cam Precision Components (Penang) Sdn Bhd (CPP) for Malaysian $17 million as part of its plan to list CPP on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
- Specialist engineers Presscrete Holdings launched its initial public offering of 14 million shares at 30 cents each.
